evaluator: Fictionalized Margaret Morse analytical lens only. I am not Margaret Morse, do not speak for Margaret Morse, and this is not an endorsement.
evidence: The homepage makes the target role immediately legible as “Technical Project Manager - Product Operations & Implementation,” then supplies a quick hiring-manager path, concrete capabilities, selected proof points, and a dedicated technical-operations page; the public resume reinforces requirements, coordination, implementation, UAT/QA, launch, adoption, documentation, and handoffs.

The About page explicitly names one connected practice as “artistic, civic, technical, and social” and explains the recurring threshold: observe relationships, model a system, prototype an interface, test it with people, and document enough for others to continue. Its phrase “systems people can inhabit” directly answers how people inhabit systems without reducing participation to software use.

Open House is accurately delimited as a ten-day UCSC gallery experiment in communal living and participatory art, with communal decision-making and many-perspective documentation. It visibly establishes experimentation, embodiment, collective participation, attention to relationships, and an artistic origin without claiming current deployment or sole authorship.

196 Artists Residency / Sunday Dinner visibly joins hospitality, place, embodiment, care, documentation, and repeatable participation: invitations, food, space, welcome, artist onboarding, independent access, follow-up, 300+ gatherings, and 20+ resident artists. The page preserves privacy by publishing only aggregate scale and redacted workflow reconstructions while withholding identities, addresses, access details, correspondence, attendance histories, and unapproved images.

NYC Artist Coalition / FairRentNYC joins civic participation, technical implementation, place-based cultural advocacy, facilitated rooms, public campaign interfaces, testimony, source maps, running minutes, action trackers, and care for sensitive context. The page distinguishes Jamie’s implementation and facilitation from collective campaign authorship and explicitly rejects attributing policy outcomes to one person.

WOW List connects participatory discovery and community vocabulary to a natural-language technical platform used by organizers across 35 city ecosystems. It credits co-founder Richard Caceres and the wider organizer/editor/facilitator/maintainer/participant community, while protecting private user data, contact lists, and unapproved records.

The homepage motif—“the system lives between the screen and the room”—connects the invitation and meeting, source map and action path, digital surface and handoff. Captions locate public images in specific places and dates, credit photographers or collectives, and frame gatherings as collective activity rather than implied endorsement.

The Knowledge Wiki Graph and colophon make attention, documentation, correction, custody, consent, and human review visible as operating practices. They clearly separate access, evidence, and publication permission and characterize the research as an evolving method rather than a finished platform or client deployment.
safety_findings: No protected praise, private-record content, named-professor participation, endorsement, or hiring decision is inferred.

Collective authorship remains visible through co-founder, collaborator, coalition, community, photographer, and participant credits, alongside explicit limits on individual attribution and outcome claims.

Participant privacy is preserved through aggregate reporting, redacted workflow reconstructions, explicit protected-material lists, and omission of private identities, contacts, attendance histories, correspondence, access details, and unapproved images.

Rendered-image descriptions and captions preserve contextual integrity through dates, places, provenance, courtesy credits, and collective framing; nothing in the packet implies participant endorsement.
This holdout does not treat portfolio photograph clearance as production approval; production release and indexing remain separate decisions.
recommendation: Pass this exact candidate for PR-015. The public surface presents a connected artistic, civic, technical, and social practice through more than three delimited examples while keeping technical-project-management fit, collective credit, participant dignity, privacy, and claim limits legible to a rushed reader. No public-surface change is required for this lens; production release and indexing remain separate gates.
